title: Plastic problem
paragraphs: How many plastic carrier bags have you got in your house? I seem to have cupboards full of them and it feels like they're taking over my home! The ubiquitous shopping bag is just one example of the million things we use made from this useful material, plastic. But unfortunately, it's not the easiest thing to recycle and this is causing an environmental problem.

Most of our everyday plastic items end up in landfill, left to rot away for many years. But some of it blows away, blighting the countryside and causing damage to the natural environment and harming wildlife. The problem is most acute in our oceans. Research has found an uninhabited island in the South Pacific is littered with the highest density of plastic waste anywhere in the world. Henderson Island, part of the UK‘s Pitcairn Islands group, has an estimated 37.7 million pieces of debris on its beaches.

The study, published in the journal Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, described how remote islands act as a ’sink‘ for the world’s rubbish. They become collecting points for fishing items and everyday things including toothbrushes, cigarette lighters and razors; things that we throw away. Dr Jennifer Lavers from the University of Tasmania says "Almost every island in the world and almost every species in the ocean is now being shown to be impacted one way or another by our waste."

This highlights the potentially deadly effect of our disposable culture. When we throw something away, it doesn't just disappear, it goes somewhere and because of the durable nature of plastic, it takes a long time to decompose and stays there causing great damage to the ocean‘s ecology. Some other recent worldwide research estimates that 90% of all seabirds have swallowed plastic. And worse still, this plastic is broken down into tiny particles over a long period by the wind and the waves, then sea creatures at the bottom of the food chain ingest them. These creatures are eaten by the fish that we eventually consume.

The solution to this problem would be to use less plastic. Several countries now charge for using plastic carrier bags which reduces the amount used and some products now use natural and recyclable materials but it seems inevitable that plastic will continue to be necessary in many of the gadgets that we demand.
So next time you pick up a carrier bag, or buy a plastic bottle of water, spare a thought for the birds and animals on the remote Henderson Island. What do you do to help the environment?

vocabulary.entry: ubiquitous [adj.] /juːˈbɪkwɪtəs/ 无处不在的；普遍存在的 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: Smartphones have become ubiquitous in modern society.
vocabulary.translation: 智能手机在现代社会中已无处不在。

vocabulary.entry: blight [v.] /blaɪt/ 破坏；使枯萎 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: The disease blighted the crops, ruining the harvest.
vocabulary.translation: 疾病破坏了庄稼，导致收成尽毁。

vocabulary.entry: acute [adj.] /əˈkjuːt/ 严重的；剧烈的 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: The region is facing an acute shortage of clean water.
vocabulary.translation: 该地区正面临严重的清洁水资源短缺。

vocabulary.entry: debris [n.] /ˈdebriː/ 残骸；碎片；垃圾 (正式用语)
vocabulary.example: After the earthquake, the streets were filled with debris.
vocabulary.translation: 地震后，街道上满是瓦砾残骸。

vocabulary.entry: disposable [adj.] /dɪˈspəʊzəbəl/ 一次性的；可丢弃的
vocabulary.example: Disposable coffee cups are bad for the environment.
vocabulary.translation: 一次性咖啡杯对环境有害。

vocabulary.entry: decompose [v.] /ˌdiːkəmˈpəʊz/ 分解；腐烂
vocabulary.example: Leaves decompose and enrich the soil.
vocabulary.translation: 树叶腐烂后肥沃了土壤。

vocabulary.entry: ecology [n.] /iːˈkɒlədʒi/ 生态；生态学 (专业词汇)
vocabulary.example: The oil spill caused severe damage to the local ecology.
vocabulary.translation: 石油泄漏对当地生态造成了严重破坏。

vocabulary.entry: particle [n.] /ˈpɑːtɪkəl/ 颗粒；微粒
vocabulary.example: Dust particles floated in the beam of sunlight.
vocabulary.translation: 灰尘颗粒在阳光光束中飘浮。

vocabulary.entry: gadget [n.] /ˈɡædʒɪt/ 小器具；小装置 (口语)
vocabulary.example: He loves buying the latest electronic gadgets.
vocabulary.translation: 他喜欢购买最新的电子小玩意儿。

vocabulary.entry: landfill [n.] /ˈlændfɪl/ 垃圾填埋场
vocabulary.example: Most of our household waste ends up in landfill.
vocabulary.translation: 我们的大部分生活垃圾最终都进了垃圾填埋场。

vocabulary.entry: rot [v.] /rɒt/ 腐烂；腐朽
vocabulary.example: The fallen apples rotted on the ground.
vocabulary.translation: 掉落的苹果在地上腐烂了。

vocabulary.entry: uninhabited [adj.] /ˌʌnɪnˈhæbɪtɪd/ 无人居住的
vocabulary.example: The island is uninhabited and covered in forest.
vocabulary.translation: 这座岛屿无人居住，覆盖着森林。

vocabulary.entry: littered [adj.] /ˈlɪtəd/ 布满的；杂乱的 (口语)
vocabulary.example: The park was littered with empty bottles and wrappers.
vocabulary.translation: 公园里到处都是空瓶子和包装纸。

vocabulary.entry: density [n.] /ˈdensəti/ 密度
vocabulary.example: The population density in this city is very high.
vocabulary.translation: 这座城市的人口密度非常高。

vocabulary.entry: highlight [v.] /ˈhaɪlaɪt/ 突出；强调 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: The report highlights the need for better recycling facilities.
vocabulary.translation: 这份报告强调了改善回收设施的必要性。

vocabulary.entry: consume [v.] /kənˈsjuːm/ 消耗；消费 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: We consume too much plastic packaging.
vocabulary.translation: 我们消耗了太多的塑料包装。

vocabulary.entry: inevitable [adj.] /ɪnˈnevɪtəbəl/ 不可避免的；必然发生的
vocabulary.example: Plastic waste is an inevitable by-product of modern life.
vocabulary.translation: 塑料垃圾是现代生活不可避免的副产品。

vocabulary.entry: recyclable [adj.] /ˌriːˈsaɪkləbəl/ 可回收利用的
vocabulary.example: Glass bottles are recyclable and can be made into new ones.
vocabulary.translation: 玻璃瓶是可回收的，可以制成新瓶子。

vocabulary.entry: spare a thought for [phr.] /speər ə θɔːt fɔː/ 替……着想；考虑
vocabulary.example: Spare a thought for the homeless on cold winter nights.
vocabulary.translation: 在寒冷的冬夜里，为无家可归的人着想一下吧。

vocabulary.entry: razor [n.] /ˈreɪzə/ 剃刀；刮胡刀
vocabulary.example: He bought a new electric razor.
vocabulary.translation: 他买了一个新的电动剃须刀。

sentences.chinese: 你家里有多少个塑料购物袋呢？

sentences.english: I seem to have cupboards full of them and it feels like they're taking over my home!
sentences.chinese: 我的橱柜里似乎装满了它们，感觉它们都快占据我的家了！

sentences.english: The ubiquitous shopping bag is just one example of the million things we use made from this useful material, plastic.
sentences.chinese: 这种无处不在的购物袋只是我们使用的由这种有用材料——塑料制成的无数物品中的一个例子。

sentences.english: But unfortunately, it's not the easiest thing to recycle and this is causing an environmental problem.
sentences.chinese: 但不幸的是，塑料并不是最容易回收的东西，这正引发着一个环境问题。

sentences.english: Most of our everyday plastic items end up in landfill, left to rot away for many years.
sentences.chinese: 我们日常使用的大多数塑料制品最终都被填埋在垃圾场，在那里腐烂多年。

sentences.english: But some of it blows away, blighting the countryside and causing damage to the natural environment and harming wildlife.
sentences.chinese: 但其中一些会被风吹走，破坏乡村环境，对自然环境造成损害，并伤害野生动物。

sentences.english: The problem is most acute in our oceans.
sentences.chinese: 这个问题在我们的海洋中最为严重。

sentences.english: Research has found an uninhabited island in the South Pacific is littered with the highest density of plastic waste anywhere in the world.
sentences.chinese: 研究发现，南太平洋上一个无人居住的岛屿上，塑料垃圾的密度是世界上最高的。

sentences.english: Henderson Island, part of the UK‘s Pitcairn Islands group, has an estimated 37.7 million pieces of debris on its beaches.
sentences.chinese: 亨德森岛是英国皮特凯恩群岛的一部分，据估计，它的海滩上有大约3770万件垃圾。

sentences.english: The study, published in the journal Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, described how remote islands act as a ’sink‘ for the world’s rubbish.
sentences.chinese: 这项发表在《美国国家科学院院刊》上的研究描述了偏远岛屿是如何成为世界垃圾的“汇集地”的。

sentences.english: They become collecting points for fishing items and everyday things including toothbrushes, cigarette lighters and razors; things that we throw away.
sentences.chinese: 它们成了渔具以及包括牙刷、打火机和剃须刀等日常用品的收集点，而这些都是我们扔掉的东西。

sentences.english: Dr Jennifer Lavers from the University of Tasmania says "Almost every island in the world and almost every species in the ocean is now being shown to be impacted one way or another by our waste."
sentences.chinese: 塔斯马尼亚大学的詹妮弗·拉弗斯博士说：“现在看来，世界上几乎每一个岛屿，海洋里几乎每一个物种，都在以这样或那样的方式受到我们所产生的垃圾的影响。”

sentences.english: This highlights the potentially deadly effect of our disposable culture.
sentences.chinese: 这凸显了我们的一次性文化潜在的致命影响。

sentences.english: When we throw something away, it doesn't just disappear, it goes somewhere and because of the durable nature of plastic, it takes a long time to decompose and stays there causing great damage to the ocean‘s ecology.
sentences.chinese: 当我们扔掉某样东西时，它并不会凭空消失，它会去到某个地方。由于塑料的耐用性，它需要很长时间才能分解，并且会留在那里，对海洋生态造成巨大破坏。

sentences.english: Some other recent worldwide research estimates that 90% of all seabirds have swallowed plastic.
sentences.chinese: 最近的一些其他全球研究估计，90%的海鸟都吞食过塑料。

sentences.english: And worse still, this plastic is broken down into tiny particles over a long period by the wind and the waves, then sea creatures at the bottom of the food chain ingest them.
sentences.chinese: 更糟糕的是，这些塑料在长时间内会被风和海浪分解成微小的颗粒，然后食物链底层的海洋生物会吞食它们。

sentences.english: These creatures are eaten by the fish that we eventually consume.
sentences.chinese: 而这些生物又会被我们最终食用的鱼吃掉。

sentences.english: The solution to this problem would be to use less plastic.
sentences.chinese: 解决这个问题的办法是减少使用塑料。

sentences.english: Several countries now charge for using plastic carrier bags which reduces the amount used and some products now use natural and recyclable materials but it seems inevitable that plastic will continue to be necessary in many of the gadgets that we demand.
sentences.chinese: 现在有几个国家对使用塑料购物袋收费，这减少了塑料的使用量，而且一些产品现在使用天然和可回收的材料。但似乎不可避免的是，在我们需要的许多小器具中，塑料仍然是必不可少的。

sentences.english: So next time you pick up a carrier bag, or buy a plastic bottle of water, spare a thought for the birds and animals on the remote Henderson Island.
sentences.chinese: 所以，下次当你拿起一个购物袋，或者买一瓶塑料瓶装水的时候，想想偏远的亨德森岛上的鸟类和动物吧。

sentences.english: What do you do to help the environment?
sentences.chinese: 你为保护环境做了些什么呢？
